text:
Justin Faulk is 34, past 1,000 NHL games, and logging a lot of minutes for a struggling Red Wings team: 22 a night over his last ten games, up two and a half from his season average. When Detroit visited St. Louis on Nov. 10, NHL.com ran a piece titled "Thank you, Justin Faulk," a nod to his years with the Blues.

The production has dried up. He has no points in five straight games, and unlike some slumps, the chances have thinned out too, and his own shot quality has been low. He has nine points in 21 games, and his scoring rate sits inside our talent range.

The underlying team numbers are close to even with him on the ice (51.6% of expected goals at five on five), and his line has scored 4.4 fewer goals than its chances, so there's a little bad luck in there. But Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 4% of defensemen for creating offense last season. He's a minutes eater on a team that lost its top center to a trade standoff. Expect steady, not spectacular.
